scope: All tracked and unignored untracked repository-owned .compact sources, including hidden paths; generated/dependency/build outputs excluded. Covers curve/public-key boundaries, not a full contract audit.
limitations: Static observations only. No compilation, contract execution, malicious witness, forged signature, attack transaction, proving, wallet UI, node submission or production deployment checked by this artifact.
No claim that every prototype compiles on the current toolchain; consult per-project compiler/version metadata.
Dependency point decoding and cryptographic primitive behavior require separate executable/source evidence in research/ecc-validation.md and existing ECC test artifacts.

explicitGuards.identity: No standalone identity assert: activation and commitment derivation extract P-256 coordinates; device/grant use additionally assert WebAuthn verifier success.
explicitGuards.subgroup: No explicit subgroup guard; P-256 has cofactor one, so native valid nonidentity curve points have prime order.
explicitGuards.pointFormat: Native Secp256r1Point coordinate extraction and webauthn_verify/p256_verify_digest are relied on; not a byte parser in this module.

validationNotes: ZswapCoinPublicKey is a coin-ownership recipient value, not the separate Ledger encryption public key. Source does not receive or validate that encryption point; output encryption is a client/Ledger boundary.
Encryption key stored as opaque Bytes<32>; fixed byte width is not a low-order or curve-validity check.
Imports/shared definitions supply WebAuthn verification and current account state helpers. Native verifier semantics are a dependency boundary, not proven by source inventory.

explicitGuards.subgroup: [8]P != O excludes pure small-order points but is not a complete prime-subgroup test for mixed-torsion points. Native point decoding/arithmetic supplies the additional boundary described in ecc-validation.md.
explicitGuards.pointFormat: K256 coordinate guard and native coordinate access/arithmetic are used; no author-written full curve-equation/encoding parser. Jubjub commitment hashes and opaque encryption bytes alone do not validate keys.

validationNotes: ZswapCoinPublicKey is a coin-ownership recipient value, not the separate Ledger encryption public key. Source does not receive or validate that encryption point; output encryption is a client/Ledger boundary.

Device/grant entries are opaque commitments: enrolment cannot validate the hidden key; activation/use gates do. Signature announcement R has no explicit nonidentity restriction. Recovery keys are checked when publishing sessions, submitting and finalising, but not at initial constructor storage. No executable test is implied by this inventory.
The comment immediately above require_live_jubjub_point claiming every write to recovery_pk passes the guard is overbroad: constructor assignment at line 376 does not.
